turns.t: Mr Haldane, thanks for coming. I've got the letter from your GP here, saying you've had sore eyes since some welding. Have I got that right?
That's about the size of it. Eye pain, mostly. Nothing dramatic.
So, eye pain since welding. Tell me how it started.
I was welding most of the afternoon on Tuesday. Or it might have been Wednesday, they've run into one another. Anyway, that night it began to feel gritty and sore.
So it came on that night, but you can't pin down whether it was Tuesday or Wednesday. That's fine, it isn't essential.
Sorry. I should have kept a note.
No need to apologise. Were you wearing your helmet with the visor down the whole time?
Mostly. I lifted it for a minute or two to check a join. Probably longer than I'd care to admit.
Thank you, that's an honest answer. Does anything make the pain worse?
Bright lights bother me. I wore sunglasses indoors yesterday, and felt daft.
Not daft, sensible. How would you rate the pain, mild, moderate, or worse?
Moderate. I can work through it, but I wouldn't want to.
Understood. Any loss of vision, or things going blurry or dark in the middle?
No, my sight's the same. Just sore.
Good. So pain, bright lights make it worse, and your sight is unchanged. Do you wear glasses?
Short-sighted, since I was a teenager. I've got my glasses in my pocket.
And does any eye trouble run in the family?
My mother had glaucoma. She lost a fair bit of her vision in the end.
I'm sorry to hear that, and thank you, it's worth knowing. What's your job, exactly?
I'm a welder at a boatyard. Twenty-two years now, so I should know better.
Twenty-two years, so you know the risks well. Before I look at the eyes properly, any allergies I should know about?
Yes, actually. I'm allergic to some kind of eye drops. I come up in a reaction, but I can't recall what it was. Years ago.
So an allergy to certain eye drops, reaction not remembered. I'll note that, and we'll steer clear of any drops until we know more.
Fine. Is the examination going to hurt?
I'll keep it gentle. First the checks we do for everyone. Pressure, pulse, temperature and oxygen.
Blood pressure is 132 over 84, pulse 70, temperature 36.7 degrees, and oxygen 99 percent.
Sounds fine to me.
It is. Now chin on the rest please, and look straight at the light. A bit of glare, I'm sorry.
Ow. That's bright.
Both eyes look red, and the surface of both looks roughened, like a freshly sanded table top.
Is that bad?
It's what I'd expect. A welder who lifted his visor, red eyes, a rough surface. That looks most like a flash burn, what we call arc eye.
And does that settle by itself? I was expecting drops or something.
It usually does, so no drops this time. I'm not prescribing anything. Cool damp cloth over closed eyes, rest, and sunglasses outdoors.
How long before I'm back at the boatyard?
Two or three days off, and no welding at all until I've seen the eyes again.
Right. That's awkward but doable. Could I drive home?
In your sunglasses, yes, but get a lift if someone can come. Do you want a note for your foreman?
Please. He likes things on paper.
I'll write that today. I'd also like to see you again in three days, to check the surface has healed.
Three days. I'll ring the boatyard and tell them.
Good. And please, always visor down, even for a quick glance at a join.
Fair point. Old habits.
So to recap: rest, a cool cloth, sunglasses, and back here in three days. Ring the clinic if the pain gets sharply worse.
Will do. Thanks, doctor.
Take care of those eyes, Mr Haldane.

physical_examination.normalized_finding: Bilateral red eyes with roughened corneal surface

clinical_actions.description: Cool damp cloth over closed eyes, rest, sunglasses outdoors, no welding until reviewed
Write a note for the employer
Always keep the visor down when welding
Ring the clinic if the pain gets sharply worse

clinical_uncertainties.description: The patient cannot say whether the eye pain began after welding on Tuesday or Wednesday.
